Tumpak Sewu, Indonesia

Deep in the rainforests of East Java, Tumpak Sewu spills over a 120-meter horseshoe-shaped cliff in dozens of slender streams. Its name means “a thousand waterfalls”—and from the jungle’s edge, the falling water does look like a vast silver veil.

The falls are fed by the Glidik River, which flows down from Mount Semeru, an active volcano. During the rainy season, the water surges and mist fills the canyon. Locals consider the site sacred, believing its waters cleanse the soul and bring good fortune.

Reaching Tumpak Sewu is part of the experience: the route winds along jungle trails, crosses bamboo bridges, and descends into the canyon. From the viewpoint above, the waterfall opens into a sweeping panorama—an unforgettable meeting of land and water. 💧
